question: Per CI DAG step, where does parallel scaling plateau or regress, and can the ci-dag runner capture the data and derive that plateau as the step's max-threads on a given machine?

instrument.note: All wall/CPU/effective_cores/peak values are the runner's own cgroup-recorded per-step profile rows. This experiment adds no external stopwatch.
instrument.wrapper_reason: The agent sandbox scope exposes cgroup.controllers='io memory pids' with no cpu controller, so cpu.max cannot be set and a sweep's width would be inert. systemd-run --user yields 'cpuset cpu io memory pids'.

method.width_order: independently shuffled per replicate; defends against ambient load drift aliasing onto the width axis
method.plateau_rule: smallest width whose median wall is within 5% of the best median
method.regression_rule: smallest width above best whose median exceeds best by >5% AND whose [min,max] range is disjoint from best's; overlapping candidates are reported 'suspected' and are not actionable
method.failed_samples: excluded from the derived table, retained in raw/

capability_demo.unit: sha256sum of the page-cached payload (~0.163 s)
capability_demo.shape: fixed total work split into exactly <width> forked workers; forks scale with width, not with unit count
capability_demo.cache_state: page-cache warm, warmed before the first sample; no cold/warm mode exists for this payload

ambient.note: Shared box with roughly 14 concurrent agents. Randomized width order and replication defend against drift aliasing onto the width axis; they do not make this an idle-host measurement.

raw_data.raw/demo-store: NEGATIVE CONTROL: first sweep, every width killed by the 10 CPU-second default cpu_timeout. Truncation times form a plausible but entirely fictitious scaling curve. Do not use as measurements.
raw_data.raw/demo-store-v2: 192-unit sweep; per-unit fork overhead floored effective_cores at ~58/316
raw_data.raw/demo-store-v3: PRIMARY: 576-unit chunked strong-scaling sweep, 13 widths x 3 reps, 39/39 valid
raw_data.raw/hermit-steps-store: three real hermit check.* steps; only check.portability_paths succeeded
raw_data.raw/collision-demo: the two datasets merged as a shared store would merge them, demonstrating Defect 5
raw_data.raw/cc-recheck: single-sample reproduction of the container_class mis-record

hermit_check_portability_paths.verdict: flat by construction, single-threaded; not a measured plateau

defects_found: 1: plateau estimator has never fired - 0 curves from 129 real rows / 52 steps; 52/52 steps have exactly one inner_jobs width vs _SPEEDUP_MIN_LEVELS=2
2: the runner's width knob cannot reach a hermit step's parallelism - default_jobs_flag is null and 19/48 portable steps hardcode --test-threads=N or CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 in the cmd string
3: plateau and cliff are indistinguishable in StepSpeedup output; the recommendation is nonetheless SAFE (greedy stop-at-first-failure never advances past a degradation)
4: the estimator ingests FAILED samples - bucketize_rows/sample_from_row never inspect ok/returncode/timed_out/oom_kills

5: container_class collides under cgroup boxing - 16-CPU container rows record affinity316, and the quota half reads the ROOT cgroup cpu.max; merged, the estimator recommends 192 threads for a 16-CPU container
6: analyze.summarize() keys on duration_s but the store writes elapsed_s; drops 100% of rows for all 52 steps
limitations: Every sample is ambient_bucket=busy; absolute walls would be lower on a quiet host

The estimator applies a contention discount: 71.278 s reported vs 94.435 s measured median at width 1 (25%). Tables report raw measured medians; only recommended_inner_jobs comes from the discounted path
1a/1b are a synthetic CPU-bound payload, not a hermit workload
Only one real hermit step swept; check.script_sigpipe (rc=2) and check.skill_discovery (rc=127, rustc absent from the transient unit PATH) failed at every width
The 12 --test-threads steps and 7 build steps were not swept: they need a full workspace build and per Defect 2 their thread counts would not move
No confirmed regression anywhere in this dataset; two suspected points fail the dispersion test
n=2 for the 16-CPU container run, n=3 elsewhere
